articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Actions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. This action underscores the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to disrupting illicit networks that pose a threat to national security.

These designations aim to sever financial and logistical support for criminal and terrorist organizations, thereby limiting their ability to operate and conduct harmful activities globally. The specific details of the designated parties and the nature of their involvement were outlined in the Treasury's official announcement.

Such measures are a critical component of broader U.S. efforts to combat international crime and terrorism, often involving coordination with international partners to maximize impact and prevent evasion.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran-Related SDN Listing for Volta Shipping Services LLC
body: On November 9, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an update to an Iran-related entry on its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. The update concerns Volta Shipping Services LLC, a UAE-based company linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

The change specifically amends the listed alias for Volta Shipping Services LLC from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO. The company remains designated under Executive Order 13902, continuing to be subject to secondary sanctions risk.

This action is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to maintain the accuracy and effectiveness of its sanctions lists and to counter Iran's illicit activities, particularly those related to its shadow fleet and efforts to evade sanctions.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canada-Based Money Services Businesses for Iran-Related Digital Asset Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight Canada-based money services businesses on November 6, 2026, for their alleged involvement in facilitating transactions for Iran's digital asset sector. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.

These businesses are accused of exchanging Iranian currency for digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The action was coordinated with FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC.

The designations were made under Executive Order 13902, which targets key sectors of the Iranian economy. This move highlights the U.S. government's focus on disrupting Iran's ability to leverage digital assets for illicit financial activities and proliferation-sensitive programs.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal / Steptoe

articles.headline: OFAC Expands Cuba Sanctions to Manufacturing, Technology, Electronics, and Marine Sectors; Designates Entities
body: On November 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine. This action significantly broadens the scope for potential future designations.

Concurrently, the U.S. designated Cuban oil shippers, Cuban state entities, and Chinese military suppliers. Among the Chinese companies sanctioned were China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation, both accused of supplying equipment to Cuba's military.

The new sanctions aim to prevent the Cuban regime from funneling resources to its military elite and to disrupt opaque offshore networks. This move increases compliance obligations and enforcement risk for companies with international operations that may have connections to these newly designated sectors in Cuba.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / World Socialist Web Site / CTV News

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: On November 4, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings, alongside the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert. This alert specifically warns against the Iranian shadow fleet's reliance on false flags for sanctions evasion.

In a related action, OFAC sanctioned four individuals and nine entities allegedly linked to an India-based network supporting Iran's shadow fleet, which provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 5AA), authorizing transactions related to, financing for, and other dealings in the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 percent bond, effective December 18, 2026. This new GL replaces and supersedes GL 5Z.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Steptoe / Federal Register

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License. This action modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Iran.

The specifics of the amendments were not immediately detailed in the brief announcement, but such changes typically aim to either narrow or broaden the scope of permissible activities under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations (ITSR).
Businesses and individuals engaged in Iran-related activities are advised to review the updated General License carefully to ensure ongoing compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These actions aim to counter illicit activities that undermine regional stability and international security.

For North Korea, the designations likely target individuals or entities involved in the regime's weapons of mass destruction programs, cyber activities, or other illicit revenue generation. In the DRC, the focus is typically on those supporting armed groups or engaging in corruption.

These designations reinforce the U.S. government's commitment to enforcing sanctions against those who threaten international peace and security, and to preventing the proliferation of dangerous technologies and the financing of conflict.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: On October 27, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. (Extreme) for apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The settlement resolves nine apparent violations arising from exports to a blocked Russian defense manufacturer between September 2018 and March 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed but egregious. The violations involved exports from the United States to JSC Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian missile manufacturer majority-owned by the sanctioned state-owned defense company JSC Concern Almaz Antey.

The compliance failures stemmed from Extreme's Russian subsidiary's purchase of customer accounts and contracts, including one naming MMZA as an end user. OFAC stated that Extreme did not conduct sufficient due diligence to recognize that MMZA was blocked, despite red flags.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs Regarding Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) concerning blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update aims to provide clearer guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations.

The amendments likely address common questions and provide updated interpretations or procedures related to the reporting of blocked property and rejected transactions, which are crucial aspects of sanctions compliance.
Entities subject to OFAC regulations are encouraged to review the updated FAQs to ensure their internal procedures align with the latest guidance, thereby mitigating the risk of non-compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. This action also included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.

The Iran-related designations are part of ongoing efforts to pressure the Iranian regime, while the removals for Belarus and North Korea may indicate specific policy adjustments or compliance by previously sanctioned entities.

The new General Licenses and amended FAQs provide updated guidance for various transactions, reflecting the dynamic nature of U.S. sanctions policy and the need for businesses to stay informed of the latest regulatory changes.

articles.headline: EU Imposes New Sanctions on 113 Individuals and Entities to Curb Russia's War Financing and 'Shadow Fleet'
body: On November 16, 2026, the European Council imposed additional restrictive measures on 12 individuals and 101 entities in response to Russia's attacks against Ukraine. These sanctions target economic sectors that provide substantial revenue to Russia's war efforts and support its 'shadow fleet'.

The new listings include nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, aiming to cut off financial channels that fund Russia's war. The package also targets Russia's e-commerce sector, including the sole shareholder of retail giant Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon.

Furthermore, the sanctions target Russia's 'shadow fleet' by listing companies from the UAE, China, Seychelles, and Oman that are buyers of Russian crude oil products, as well as businesspersons involved in the illegal transportation of Russian oil through high-risk shipping activities.

articles.headline: EU Sanctions 30 Individuals and Two Entities for Russia's FIMI and Malicious Cyber Activities
body: On November 16, 2026, the Council of the European Union decided to add 30 individuals and two entities to the list of those subject to EU restrictive measures for their involvement in Russia's foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) and malicious cyber activities.

Among the newly listed entities is the Social Design Agency (SDA), a Moscow-based public relations and political technology company accused of carrying out large-scale information manipulation and interference projects funded and directed by the Russian Presidential Administration.

These sanctions target individuals and entities responsible for Russia's hybrid activities against third countries and international organizations, imposing asset freezes and travel bans. The EU reaffirmed its commitment to promoting an open, free, stable, and secure cyberspace.

articles.headline: EU Autumn 2026 Economic Forecast Predicts Continued Growth Amid Higher Inflation
body: The EU's Autumn 2026 Economic Forecast indicates continued economic growth, with the rate of expansion for the EU economy over the first three quarters of the year being higher than expected. However, this growth is accompanied by persistent inflationary pressures.

Annual inflation in the EU is projected to reach 3.3% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, before moderating to 2.3% in 2028. Euro area inflation is expected to follow similar dynamics. Lower-income households are particularly exposed to high food prices and rising household energy bills.

Despite these renewed inflationary pressures, medium-term market-based inflation expectations have remained well anchored, reflecting confidence in the European Central Bank's ability to maintain price stability.

articles.headline: BIS Implements New Controls on Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors and Adds Five Countries to License Requirement
body: On November 16, 2026, the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule, 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,' which will go into effect on November 19. This rule aims to close a perceived gap in existing chip controls, preventing foreign actors from leveraging U.S.-designed computing power from data centers in third countries without a license.

A new data center end-use control will require a license to export, re-export, or transfer (in-country) advanced chips and servers if the exporter has knowledge that the item is destined for a data center providing access to more than 12 million 'aggregate TPP' to or for companies headquartered in China, Country Group D:5 destinations (including Belarus and Russia), or Macau.

Additionally, new license requirements are being imposed for exports, re-exports, or in-country transfers of advanced semiconductors to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. These countries are deemed to present a 'higher-than-normal risk of diversion.'
articles.source: Reed Smith LLP / Mothership.SG / New Straits Times

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors, Shifting to EAR
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR). This marks a shift from the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.
This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with the controls already applied to firearms, streamlining the regulatory framework for these items.
The change is intended to simplify the export process for certain sound suppressors while maintaining appropriate national security and foreign policy considerations under the EAR.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
